review_notes: I read the whole target file. I compared it with `TM.seqTM_reachesIn_of_reachesIn` (Combinators/Internal/Seq.lean), `TM.phaseTransition_eq_self_of_reads_ne_start` (Hoare.lean), `TM.phaseTransition_of_parked` (Registers.lean) and `TM.seqTM_hoareTime`. I also read the near-identical `DenseDecisionProof.lean` and grepped for other uses of `phaseTransition_eq_self_of_reads_ne_start`. There are about 50 call sites across the library, many in the same shape. The `*_ramRun_internal` theorem has no meaningful repetition. Uncertainty: I could not compile anything. In the second use, `htailReach` starts at `phase1Wrap ...` and the helper's `hreach₂` expects the literal `qstart` config. The original closes that gap with `simpa ... using!`, so the rewritten call may still need `by simpa using! htailReach` or `convert`. The helper's rewrite step may also need a `Cfg` extensionality step. A helper stated with `Parked` hypotheses would instead reuse `TM.phaseTransition_of_parked`.

findings.problem: The proof crosses a `seqTM` seam twice (loop→output at lines 85–98, init→(loop;output) at lines 116–134) with the same reasoning. Each time it (1) shows the three tape-read facts, (2) calls `phaseTransition_eq_self_of_reads_ne_start`, (3) uses `simpa only [hi, hw, ho]` to rewrite the `transitionInput`/`transitionTape` start config of the second machine to the raw tapes, and (4) feeds the result to `seqTM_reachesIn_of_reachesIn`. Each seam also restates a long `{ state := ... qstart, input := TM.transitionInput ..., work := fun i => TM.transitionTape ..., output := ... }` literal. `DenseDecisionProof.lean` repeats the same blocks (lines 93–142), and the library has about 50 further call sites of `phaseTransition_eq_self_of_reads_ne_start` in the same shape. The seam-crossing argument is therefore copied rather than named, and any change to the seam representation has to be made in every copy.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to `seqTM_reachesIn_of_reachesIn` (it can live in Hoare.lean, which has both ingredients):

theorem TM.seqTM_reachesIn_of_reachesIn_of_reads_ne_start (tm₁ tm₂ : TM n) {t₁ t₂ : ℕ} {c₁_start c₁_end : Cfg n tm₁.Q} {c₂_end : Cfg n tm₂.Q} (hreach₁ : tm₁.reachesIn t₁ c₁_start c₁_end) (hhalt₁ : c₁_end.state = tm₁.qhalt) (hinp : c₁_end.input.read ≠ Γ.start) (hwork : ∀ i, (c₁_end.work i).read ≠ Γ.start) (hout : c₁_end.output.read ≠ Γ.start) (hreach₂ : tm₂.reachesIn t₂ { state := tm₂.qstart, input := c₁_end.input, work := c₁_end.work, output := c₁_end.output } c₂_end) : (seqTM tm₁ tm₂).reachesIn (t₁ + 1 + t₂) (phase1Wrap tm₁ tm₂ c₁_start) (phase2Wrap tm₁ tm₂ c₂_end)

Proof sketch: `obtain ⟨hi, hw, ho⟩ := phaseTransition_eq_self_of_reads_ne_start hinp hwork hout`, then `exact seqTM_reachesIn_of_reachesIn tm₁ tm₂ hreach₁ hhalt₁ (by rw [hi, hw, ho]; exact hreach₂)`.

Rewritten uses here:
1. Lines 85–98 become `have htailReach := TM.seqTM_reachesIn_of_reachesIn_of_reads_ne_start (programLoopTM tapes program) (programOutputTM tapes) hloopReach hloopHalt hloopInputParked.read_ne_start (fun i => (hloopReady.control.lookup.scanner.parked i).read_ne_start) hloopOutputParked.read_ne_start houtputReach`. The `houtputReach'` literal disappears.
2. Lines 116–134 become `have hreach := TM.seqTM_reachesIn_of_reachesIn_of_reads_ne_start (programInitTM tapes) (TM.seqTM (programLoopTM tapes program) (programOutputTM tapes)) hinitReach hinitHalt hinitInputParked.read_ne_start (fun i => (hinitWorkParked i).read_ne_start) hinitOutputParked.read_ne_start (by simpa using! htailReach)`. The `by simpa using!` argument stands in for the original `htailReach'`, because `htailReach` starts at `phase1Wrap` of the loop config. The `htailReach'` literal disappears.

The same lemma also replaces the duplicated blocks in `DenseDecisionProof.lean`.
findings.benefit: This removes two roughly 15-line blocks with large config literals from this proof, and the same two blocks from the dense version. It leaves the real content visible: loop, then output, with every tape parked at the seams. It also gives one place to maintain the seam argument. It is more than a thin wrapper, because it fuses the `phaseTransition` identification with the start-config rewrite and the `seqTM` reachability, and these steps currently appear together in every such proof.
